This second application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.05 of 2022 registered at Police Station- Cyber Cell, District Gwalior (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468,
471, 204 of IPC and added Sections 66- C, and 66-D of I.T. Act .

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Applicant is in judicial custody since 19.10.2022.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn by Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 22.02.2024 passed in MCRC No.650/2024.

As per the case of prosecution, Sudhish Singh Tomar submitted a written complaint on 17.11.2021 to the Superintendent of Police, State Cyber Police Zone, Gwalior with regard to fraudulent withdrawn of Rs.6,23,989/- from the account of his father Tehsildar Singh Tomar in SBI, Morena Branch.
It is stated in the complaint that Tehsildar Singh Tomar, retired Teacher has an account in SBI, Morena Branch, wherein his pension is regularly deposited.
Tehsildar Singh found that Rs.6,23,989/- has been withdrawn from his account without any intimation.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:13635 2 MCRC-20526-2024
On such allegations, the matter was enquired.

It was found that the amount was transferred into the account of Dilshad,
Samad, Farooz, Ruksina and Harjeet.
Dilshad was arrested on 20.08.2022.

He informed in his statement recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act that Tehrim S/o Irfhan used to provide Vivek Kumar Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24343750/
1 him mobile SIMs registered in fake names and using these mobile SIMs, he used to call innocent depositors and withdraw amount from their bank accounts.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rajat Lodhi was arrested on 18.10.2022.
Rajat Lodhi in his statement recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act informed that Chandrashekhar @ Chandu, Namdev and Vivek Kumar (applicant) were working as agents of Vodafone and Idea.
He approached Chandrashekar and Vivek for issuance of SIM in fake names.
Chandrashekhar and Vivek provided him SIMs issued registered in fake names.
He gave those SIMS to Tehrim.
Tehrim paid him Rs.1,10,000/- out of which, he has paid Rs.20,000/- each to Vivek and Chandrashekhar.
Accordingly, Vivek was arrested on 19.10.2022.
In his statement recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act, he informed that he used to register mobile SIM of Vodafone and Idea and provide them to Rajat Lodhi.
Applicant is in judicial custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted.
The trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter merely on suspicion and for issuance of SIM.
Applicant has issued SIM, but he was not aware of alleged offence.
He never came in contact with main accused Tehrim and Dilshad.
No offence as alleged is made out against applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that all material witnesses have been examined.
There is no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence by applicant.
Applicant has already undergone custody for one year and ten months.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:13635 3 MCRC-20526-2024
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 31 years and is labourer by profession.
He is sole bread earner of the family, therefore, there is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family and home.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the applicant.
The trial would take time to complete.
Co-accused Chandrashekhar has been extended benefit of bail by this Court vide order dated 15.07.2024 passed in MCRC No.18393/2024.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant- Vivek Kumar Sen shall be released on bail in relation to Crime No.05 of 2022 registered at Police Station- Cyber Cell, District Gwalior (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 204 of IPC and added Sections 66-C, and 66-D of I.T.
